business_scope.primary_industry_name: Product Interface Design and Digital Design Subscription Agency

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Mainland China (WFOE registered seat); Taiwan (TW) as investor-origin sub-state under PRC unitary sovereignty
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement (ECFA) between the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits and the Straits Exchange Foundation (2010)
Cross-Strait Agreement on the Avoidance of Double Taxation and Enhancement of Tax Cooperation (2015)
Cross-Strait Agreement on Securing and Authentication of Notarized Documents (1993)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (revised 2024, effective 1 January 2025); Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information in Financial Institutions and Specific Non-Financial Institutions (PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3, effective 1 November 2024); Company Law of the PRC; Foreign Investment Law of the PRC (2019); Law of the PRC on the Protection of Investment by Compatriots from Taiwan (2019 amendment); Provisions on the Administration of Enterprise Name Registration (State Council Order No. 734); Regulations on the Registration Administration of Market Entities (State Council Order No. 746).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Taiwan corporate investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization only: Taiwan district court notarization; authentication by Taiwan Bureau of Consular Affairs; verification by Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) and Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS); submission to SAMR. Hague Apostille is not available and is never chained with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the Taiwan corporate investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization only: Taiwan notarization; Taiwan foreign affairs authentication; SEF/ARATS cross-strait verification; submission to PRC authorities. Hague Apostille is not available for Taiwan-origin instruments and must not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney appointing the WFOE legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan investor board of directors, notarized by a Taiwan district court notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization path for Taiwan execution; if executed and notarized in an Apostille Convention state, a single Hague Apostille is used independently. The two authentication paths are mutually exclusive and never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (constitutional documents) of the Taiwan corporate investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization only: Taiwan notarization; SEF/ARATS verification; PRC acceptance. Hague Apostille cannot be applied to Taiwan-government-issued instruments and is not chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter from the Taiwan investor's principal bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Principal commercial bank of the Taiwan investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization only: bank signatory capacity notarized in Taiwan; bank seal and signature authenticated; SEF/ARATS cross-strait verification; final submission to the WFOE's PRC bank and SAMR. Apostille route is excluded for Taiwan-origin letters.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, legal representatives, and the Taiwan-origin corporate investor must be screened against the PBOC adverse and dishonesty lists, PRC financial sanctions and terrorist designation lists, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, and OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) and non-SDN sanctions lists, because USD payment rails and correspondent-bank denials create extraterritorial exposure. PEP checks must cover domestic and foreign political exposure, family members, close associates, state-owned-enterprise roles, and adverse media. Enhanced due diligence applies to any beneficial owner holding 25% or more through layered trusts, nominees, or holding companies, including piercing every intermediate entity to the natural person.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) Enterprise Name Self-Service Declaration System and the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The WFOE legal name must be in simplified Chinese characters. The Taiwan investor's corporate name is transliterated into a distinctive Chinese character mark using official pinyin rules. The mandatory four-tier name order is: administrative division + distinctive name + industry description + organizational form. For ISIC 7410, the industry description must match the SAMR-approved business scope for professional design and digital design services; an English-only legal name is not accepted, though an English supplemental name may be registered.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection the applicant must obtain a written refusal reason through the name declaration system, may modify and resubmit the name immediately, and may file an administrative reconsideration request with the provincial market regulation bureau within 60 days of the refusal. The provincial SAMR must decide within 30 working days. If reconsideration is denied, the applicant may file an administrative lawsuit with the competent people's court within six months of the reconsideration decision. Alternatively, the applicant may select a new distinctive name or adjusted industry token and begin a new name reservation while preserving the right to separately appeal the underlying rejection.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible for a WFOE in this industry. Chinese market registration rules require an actual, physical, fixed business domicile; tax authorities require a physical presence before issuing normal invoice quotas; and PBOC-licensed banks require on-site inspection of business premises before opening a basic deposit account. Government-approved cluster addresses or incubation addresses are acceptable only when they constitute real office venues, not mailboxes. For a UI/UX Design-as-a-Service subscription agency, online payment concentration from Stripe and Wise will trigger VAT inspection and merchant-compliance verification, making a mailbox-only address operationally and legally fatal.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced on-site inspection: lease or ownership certificate, utility invoices, on-site employees and social insurance records, computers and design software, domain and subscription data, client agreements, bank statements, and AML/KYC files. Quantified risk: 20-25% probability of an unannounced SAMR or local tax inspection in the first 12 months for a standard WFOE with a real office; the probability exceeds 80% if no physical presence is found or if the registered address is a virtual mailbox, with potential revocation of tax registration and business license.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory official registration fee; government registry fee is zero

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Chinese translation of investor constitutional documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market tariff of USD 0.10-0.15 per Chinese character; fixed fee estimate

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Republic of China (Taiwan) Companies Act, particularly Articles 1, 2, 6, 15, 128-130, 154, 161, 172, 192, 208, 218, and 228 governing company incorporation, share capital, directors, statutory officers, and registration; Foreign Investment Act, Articles 3, 8, and 10; and the Company Name and Business Scope Review Guidelines.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commercial Services, Company Registration Division.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation and Company Registration Application Form
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None - no statutory minimum paid-up capital under the Taiwan Companies Act. However, the subscribed capital must be paid into a blocked Taiwan escrow bank account and certified by a licensed certified public accountant before the incorporation filing is submitted. The capital may not be released to management or shareholders prior to issuance of the Company Registration Certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF CN WFOE LIMITED, A COMPANY FORMED UNDER THE COMPANIES ACT OF THE REPUBLIC OF CHINA (TAIWAN). The undersigned, acting as the sole incorporator and first director of CN WFOE Limited (the Company), hereby waives formal notice of the first meeting and adopts the following resolutions, effective immediately upon the issuance of the Company Registration Certificate by the Ministry of Economic Affairs. 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: RESOLVED, that the Company's authorized share capital is [number of shares] ordinary shares at [par value or no-par stated value] per share, divided into [number of subscribed shares]; that the sole shareholder subscribes for and will pay in full the subscribed shares; that the paid-in capital shall be lodged in a segregated Taiwan bank account in the Company's name pending registration; that such funds shall remain blocked until a licensed certified public accountant issues a capital verification report; and that the capital may not be released to management until the Company's registration is conclusively approved. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: RESOLVED, that the Company shall open corporate current accounts, foreign currency accounts, and such ancillary accounts as may be required with a bank licensed in Taiwan; that the Chairperson, the sole director, and the General Manager, acting severally, are hereby authorized to execute all bank account documents, signatory cards, wire transfer instructions, foreign exchange settlement documents, and related banking agreements on behalf of the Company. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: RESOLVED, that the registered office and principal place of business of the Company is hereby fixed at [full address], Taiwan, effective as of the date of incorporation; that the registered office is a physical commercial address suitable for the service of process; and that all statutory corporate records, including the share registry, minute book, and seal records, shall be maintained at such address. 4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS: RESOLVED, that [name] is appointed as Chairperson and Director; that [name] is appointed as General Manager and the Company's legal representative for daily business operations; that [name] is appointed as Corporate Secretary with responsibility for maintaining statutory registers and minutes; and that [name] is appointed as the Company's Taiwan tax filing representative for business registration and tax compliance purposes, each to serve until removed or replaced by a duly adopted resolution. 5. GENERAL AUTHORITY: RESOLVED, that the officers and agents of the Company are hereby authorized, jointly and severally, to execute all filings, pay all official fees, procure notarizations and translations, open bank accounts, and take all actions necessary to complete the incorporation, tax registration, and lawful commencement of the Company's UI/UX design subscription services. These resolutions are adopted as the valid and binding acts of the Company, conditional upon and effective as of the Company's incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reservation of Company Name and Approval of Business Scope
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commercial Services - Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Registration Online System.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the company name reservation application for CN WFOE Limited and describe the proposed business scope as product interface design, UI/UX design, and digital design subscription agency services, referencing ISIC 7410 and NAICS 541430. The filing must indicate that the entity will be a limited liability company with one non-resident corporate shareholder. The MOEA online portal screens the proposed name against existing registered companies and rejects identical or confusingly similar names. The approved name reservation is valid for six months and the business scope must match the intended activities, including the use of Stripe Billing and Wise as payment rails. If the name is approved, the reservation certificate is used in the subsequent incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Proposed business scope description with ISIC code
Identity or incorporation certificate of the proposed shareholder
Power of attorney if the filing is made through a formation agent
Proposed company name and Chinese name-stamping slip, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to conflict, obscenity, or misleading wording, the applicant may file a corrected name reservation online without losing the original queue date. A formal written appeal may be lodged with the MOEA Department within 30 days of the rejection, followed by administrative litigation in the Taipei High Administrative Court if the appeal is denied.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Non-Resident Investment Approval by the Investment Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (Taiwan) - Foreign Investment and Mainland Investment Application Desk.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the investment approval application to the Investment Commission before remitting capital or incorporating. The application must state the total investment amount, shareholding percentage, source of funds, and intended business activity as a UI/UX design subscription agency. The Investment Commission will screen the industry for foreign investment restrictions, review the investor background, and verify that the proposed business scope is permissible under the positive list if the investor is from the mainland. The Commission will issue an Investment Approval Letter, which is required for bank remittance and company registration. The approval letter must be tendered to the bank and to MOEA at the respective stages. Any subsequent change in investor identity, business scope, or capital structure requires a new approval application or an amendment application.
required_dossiers: Investment Commission application form
Certified copy of the investor's certificate of incorporation or passport
Audited financial statements or bank reference letter for the investor
Board or shareholder resolution authorizing the investment
Proposed articles of incorporation of the Taiwan company
Legalized or notarized foreign corporate documents translated into English or Chinese
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Investment Commission issues a deficiency notice, respond fully within 30 days with certified translations and evidence of the source of funds. A rejection may be challenged by filing an administrative appeal with the Executive Yuan within 30 days of receipt, and thereafter through administrative litigation under the Administrative Litigation Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Escrow Account Opening and Certified Public Accountant Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed bank in Taiwan and a certified public accountant registered with the National Taxation Bureau of Taiwan.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Investment Approval Letter, open a temporary escrow account in the name of the proposed company at a licensed bank in Taiwan. Deposit the full subscribed paid-in capital by international wire transfer from the non-resident shareholder, using the registered name of the company and identifying the investment approval number. The bank will issue a remittance certificate and a deposit confirmation. Engage a certified public accountant to examine the bank statement, foreign exchange settlement form, deposit vouchers, and the source-of-funds declaration. The CPA must confirm that the capital is genuine and not withdrawn from other Taiwan sources, then issue a formal Capital Verification Report. The funds must remain blocked until MOEA has issued the Company Registration Certificate, and no disbursements may be made except for permitted formation expenses with supporting vouchers.
required_dossiers: Investment approval letter
Draft articles of incorporation
Bank account opening application and signatory card
Passport or corporate certificate of the funding shareholder
Source of funds declaration and wire transfer instruction
Certified public accountant capital verification report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the remittance, provide the Investment Approval Letter and a notarized source-of-funds declaration. If the CPA cannot certify the capital because of missing remittance details, request the bank to issue a corrected remittance certificate and re-verify within the escrow period. The capital cannot be used for operations before the registration certificate is issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Filing with the Ministry of Economic Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commercial Services - Company Registration Division.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the formal incorporation application through MOEA's company registration system after securing the name reservation, investment approval, and capital verification report. The filing must include the signed articles of incorporation, first board resolutions, the CPA report, the remote lease or ownership proof for the registered office, consents of the appointed directors and statutory officers, and the name reservation certificate. MOEA will verify the company name, examine the legality of the articles, confirm the capital deposit, and issue the Company Registration Certificate. The company exists as a juridical person only upon issuance of this certificate. The entire dossier must be uploaded in the prescribed digital format with certified translations for foreign documents. The examiner may request supplementary documents or clarification before passing the application for final approval.
required_dossiers: Company registration application form
Articles of incorporation signed or stamped by shareholders and directors
First board resolution adopted by the sole incorporator
CPA capital verification report and bank certificate
Investment approval letter
Registered office lease or certificate of address usage
Director and officer appointment consent forms
Company name reservation certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOEA issues a correction or query notice, rectify the stated deficiencies within the statutory period, normally 30 days, and resubmit by uploading a revised form with a written explanation. If the application is rejected, the company may appeal the decision to the Ministry of Economic Affairs under the Administrative Appeal Act and, if necessary, initiate administrative litigation in the high administrative court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Uniform Invoice Number, and Post-Incorporation Administrative Completion
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau (Ministry of Finance) and the local municipal commercial address registration desk.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within fifteen days of company registration, file the corporate tax registration with the National Taxation Bureau at the registered office location and apply for the Uniform Invoice Number, also known as the unified corporate identity number. The tax authority will enter the company into the taxpayer registry, assign the VAT filing cycle, and issue the business registration record. After receiving the Uniform Invoice Number, open the final operating corporate bank account and update the company's payment information for Stripe Billing and Wise. The company must display the Company Registration Certificate and the Uniform Invoice Number on invoices, receipts, and the design subscription billing portal. Because the business is a digital and consulting service under ISIC 7410, no sectoral operating license from an industrial authority is required. The tax registration process is ministerial and may be completed through the business startup one-stop portal.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate
Articles of incorporation and first board resolution
Uniform Invoice application form
Registered office lease and proof of commercial zoning
Fire safety equipment inspection certificate for the office
Tax representative identity document and appointment letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Taxation Bureau delays the Uniform Invoice issuance, submit a written complaint to the local tax bureau and request expedited handling under the Administrative Service Act. If the registration is rejected, amend the tax registration form by providing corrected office address or representative information and appeal to the Ministry of Finance for administrative review.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no industrial licensing board mandate is triggered for ISIC 7410 UI/UX design subscription services, as the business does not involve physical manufacturing, chemical handling, assembly, or warehousing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no separate operating or manufacturing permit is required; the Company Registration Certificate and the Uniform Invoice Number constitute the sole operating and tax authorization for the digital design subscription business.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - Exempt from Environmental Impact Assessment. ISIC 7410 is a non-industrial digital design and subscription service with no construction, manufacturing, chemical, or physical production activity, and therefore no EIA report, environmental registration, or pollution permitting requirement applies.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - zero wastewater discharge, zero VOC emissions, zero stationary emission sources, and zero hazardous waste generation from the UI/UX design operations. Office electronic waste, batteries, and discarded computer equipment must be recycled in accordance with the Taiwan Waste Disposal Act and the Recycling Management Regulations; the only quantitative compliance target is the statutory obligation to maintain office equipment with no environmental discharge.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for industrial Civil Defense fire permits because no industrial processes or stored hazardous materials exist at the registered office. The office space must, however, comply with the Taiwan Occupational Safety and Health Act and the Fire Services Act fire safety requirements, including functional fire extinguishers, emergency exit accessibility, structural load safety inspection certificates for the leased office, and a building fire safety inspection certificate before employees occupy the workspace.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, Taxation Administration, and the five regional National Taxation Bureaus; online e-Tax Portal (etax.nat.gov.tw) and E-Invoice Integrated Service Platform (einvoice.nat.gov.tw)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the Taiwan-incorporated WFOE, the Company Registry's One-Stop Online Company Registration automatically assigns a Unified Business Number (UBIN), which functions as the enterprise TIN for income tax and business tax; the National Taxation Bureau completes tax registration based on the company registration record, and no separate TIN application is needed. For a non-resident foreign enterprise that lacks a fixed place of business and sells cross-border electronic services to Taiwan consumers, the foreign entity must apply for a special Taiwan Tax ID Number by using the Ministry of Finance Cross-Border Electronic Services Tax Registration portal or by filing the statutory Application for Tax Registration with the competent National Taxation Bureau, submitting: certificate of incorporation or equivalent legal existence document, board resolution and power of attorney designating a local tax agent, a description of the Taiwan activities and digital service delivery model, and projected annual Taiwan sales. The tax authority then registers the foreign enterprise and issues a Taiwan Tax ID Number for VAT filing and payment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Taiwan does not provide check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch entity classification elections. A foreign-owned limited-liability company is mandatorily taxed as a separate corporate taxpayer; it cannot elect pass-through treatment. A fiscal-year election may be approved by the tax authority for legitimate business reasons, but that election does not alter tax entity classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Business Tax (VAT) under the Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory business tax registration before commencement for all Taiwan business entities; no general turnover threshold for a newly incorporated WFOE. Small-scale businesses with monthly taxable sales below NT$80,000 may be exempt from registration and VAT filing. A non-resident foreign electronic-service provider must register for Taiwan VAT when its annual Taiwan electronic-service sales exceed NT$480,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The WFOE must issue statutory Uniform Invoices for every domestic taxable sale. If electronic invoices are used, the entity must use the Ministry of Finance e-Invoice Turnkey and transmit the invoice data to the E-Invoice Integrated Service Platform in the prescribed format; Taiwan does not operate a mainland-China-style real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamp for all invoices, but e-invoice numbers are allocated centrally and data is used for anti-fraud reconciliation. Foreign electronic-service providers registered for Taiwan VAT must issue electronic Uniform Invoices to consumers or provide an equivalent record to the tax authority for each transaction.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 7 of the Business Tax Act, zero-rating applies to goods exported from Taiwan and to services provided to foreign clients that are used or consumed outside Taiwan. For the UI/UX design subscription service, zero-rating is available when the customer is a non-Taiwan or non-resident party, the design deliverables are delivered and used outside Taiwan, no Taiwan domestic consumption occurs, and the consideration is paid in foreign currency and repatriated to Taiwan. The service must be a genuine cross-border supply, not a Taiwan domestic use of the design product.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration for any physical/hard-copy deliverables; not applicable to pure digital design subscriptions
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill for physical deliverables; not required for pure services
Executed design-subscription contract or master service agreement identifying the foreign customer, service scope, and delivery terms
Commercial invoice or service-revenue statement in the foreign customer's name
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank foreign-exchange settlement record (SWIFT MT103 equivalent) evidencing receipt of foreign-currency proceeds
Foreign-use substantiation such as client acceptance sign-off, user location logs, or offshore hosting/delivery records demonstrating that the design service is used outside Taiwan
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the export zero-rating documentation is incomplete, the zero-rating is disallowed and the WFOE is assessed 5% output VAT on the full consideration, plus a late-payment surcharge and interest. Foreign-exchange proceeds that are not repatriated to Taiwan within 180 days of an invoice/payment are treated as evidence that the service was not genuinely exported and may trigger a retrospective VAT assessment. The ordinary tax assessment period is five years, extended to seven years for fraudulent evasion. False invoices, forged customs declarations, or artificial arrangements used to claim export zero-rating attract penalties under Article 51 of the Business Tax Act of 1 to 5 times the tax evaded, potential cancellation of registration, and criminal referral for tax fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) under the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The People's Republic of China operates a managed floating exchange rate regime with strict current account convertibility and capital account restrictions. For a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) engaged in UI/UX design subscription services, the current account (including service trade payments, royalty fees, and design subscription fees) is generally freely convertible provided that the transaction is genuine, documented, and complies with the SAFE registration requirements. However, capital account items such as inbound equity injections, foreign debt (external loans), and cross-border guarantees remain subject to SAFE registration, approval thresholds, and the Foreign Debt Macro Prudential Regulation. Export proceeds from design services are not subject to a mandatory surrender requirement under the current SAFE framework, but any receipt of foreign exchange must be settled into RMB through a designated bank with supporting contracts, invoices, and service trade declarations. Profit remittance by the WFOE to its offshore shareholder requires an annual audit report, tax clearance certificate, board resolution declaring dividends from accumulated after-tax profits, and SAFE verification via the bank's digital capital project port. The SAFE Foreign Exchange Account System and the banks' compliance screening will also scrutinize any transaction that exceeds the designated amount threshold, and the beneficiary and remitter names must align exactly with the registered entity documents. Practical hurdles include pricing reasonableness reviews for intragroup service fees, transfer pricing documentation requirements under CIT Article 41, and potential delays if the WFOE has not completed the SAFE foreign investment payment record or the annual investment report via the Ministry of Commerce system.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under current Chinese foreign exchange regulations, there is no mandatory export proceeds surrender requirement since the foreign exchange settlement system was liberalized. For service trade export receipts, the WFOE must settle foreign currency into RMB within the normal banking timeline via a designated bank after submitting the service trade foreign payment/collection application, contract, invoice, proof of service delivery, and any applicable tax vouchers. The conversion ratio is 100% at the market-driven onshore rate, with no forced retention percentage.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (RMB) and Foreign Currency Deposit Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of China (BOC) - Head Office Banking Department
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (FDI Settlement Account) and Foreign Currency Deposit Account
Basic Operational Currency Account and Service Trade Current Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability. Non-bank fintech EMIs and offshore digital banks are not legally permitted to act as primary banking service providers for Chinese onshore incorporated WFOEs. The WFOE must maintain its primary corporate banking relationship with a SAFE-designated domestic commercial bank. Offshore EMIs such as Stripe Treasury or Wise Platform cannot replace the domestic bank account for capital injection, SAFE registration, RMB settlement, or tax payments. They may be use merely as downstream collection tools for overseas subscriptions if the funds are ultimately repatriated through compliant cross-border payment service providers, but reliance on them as a settlement rail is legally constrained by PBOC payment regulations and the prohibition on circumventing SAFE monitoring.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a CN WFOE with Taiwan jurisdiction parent, the statutory legal representative, board director, and authorized financial officer must appear physically in-branch for the initial KYC interview at the domestic commercial bank if the bank's risk control policy requires face-to-face verification. Remote consular proxy opening is generally not permitted for new foreign-invested entities. Some banks allow a notarized power of attorney if the legal representative is outside mainland China, but the on-site finance manager must still attend in person with original company chops, resolution, and passport. The Taiwan shareholder documents must be authenticated by a Taiwan notary and then cross-validated under applicable cross-strait rules, which may involve additional scrutiny.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity: Taiwan-derived shareholders may obscure ultimate natural persons behind nominees or holding layers, triggering enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the full corporate ownership chain from the Taiwan ultimate beneficial owners to the CN WFOE, including notarized certificates of incorporation, articles of association, a share register, a declaration of beneficial ownership signed by each UBO, and passport copies authenticated in Taiwan and cross-strait notarized. Also submit an audited net worth statement for each 25%+ shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intangible service revenue mismatch: UI/UX design subscription payments from foreign clients may lack a clear paper trail or tangible evidence of service delivery, triggering trade falsification concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain a service delivery evidence bundle containing SOWs, client sign-off emails, screen recordings of the SaaS design platform, anti-bribery declarations, and a detailed economic substance manual. Submit invoices, receipts, a software or design asset license register, and a monthly revenue recognition schedule aligned with IT service export declarations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual transaction geometry: Frequent incoming subscription fees from Stripe/Wise aggregators and upwards profit distributions to Taiwan may trigger structuring red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Execute a standard treasury policy: every inbound payment must be mapped to the customer subscription ledger; provide bank statements from the PSP aggregators, a breakdown of settled funds, and a real-time reconciliation file. For outbound distributions, submit the audited annual financial statements, a board resolution declaring dividends, and SAFE tax clearance proof.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-jurisdictional identity matching failure: the Taiwan entity's company name may be romanized with a variant spelling, causing a mismatch at the Chinese bank's AML name screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Obtain a legal entity identifier (LEI) or corporate registry certification showing all aliases, a certificate of good standing, a certificate of incumbency, and a notarized statement confirming that the Taiwanese entity has no sanctions or adverse media nexus.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Taiwan shareholder must remit the paid-in capital via SWIFT MT103 to the WFOE's FDI capital settlement account at a designated domestic bank. The remittance purpose must be labeled as 'Investment Capital' and reference the FDI (Foreign Direct Investment) certificate. The funds must not enter a regular operational account; instead they are held in the FDI capital account. Upon settlement, the bank verifies the capital injection against the SAFE registration record and the certificate of payment. After the bank completes the foreign exchange settlement, the RMB funds can only be placed into a legally restricted RMB capital account. Then, to use the funds for business operations, the company submits a capital verification report issued by a registered CPA, the audit report, and real expense invoices such as salaries, rent, and subscriptions. The SAFE digital registry must be matched, and the bank will check that the settlement is for the actual operation of the WFOE and not for securities investment or real estate, which are prohibited. A tax filing for stamp duty on capital increase may be triggered and paid prior to disbursement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound trade payments, the preferred rails are (1) direct SWIFT MT103 wires for service fee remittances such as software vendor payments and licensing fees, using the service trade code and bank SAFE validation; (2) commercial letters of credit are not relevant for the UI/UX design service subscription model because services are not goods; (3) documentary collections are used only when the counterparty requires a bank-mediated document flow, but for a SaaS design subscription this is rare. The WFOE will mainly use the bank's 'Single Window for Trade' portal to upload the service trade contract, the invoice, a tax certificate for cross-border service payment, and the actual service completion certificate. In case of any outbound subscription royalty to the Taiwan parent to cover its own costs, a cross-border service transaction must be supported by a genuinely executed intra-group services agreement and transfer pricing documentation. The bank will perform real-time SAFE reporting and may require a payment approval letter for amounts above USD 50,000.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore CNY forward contracts with maturity no more than 12 months for genuine current account exposures, requiring a real underlying transaction and 10-15% margin or credit facility
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permitted onshore in China for WFOEs; only offshore counterparties may quote NDFs but onshore banks may only offer deliverable forwards
Cross-currency swaps are permitted for hedging foreign debt principal and interest, but only with SAFE registration and actual exposure; speculating is prohibited
FX options with zero premium structures are carefully restricted and must be justified by real trade exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business Report, Financial Statements and Shareholders' Meeting Minutes (approved and registered)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (Department of Commercial Affairs), Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The annual general meeting must be convened within six months of the fiscal year end (by 30 June for a 31 December year end); the approved business report, financial statements, and meeting minutes must be filed with the MOEA within fifteen days after the shareholders' resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is subject to a fine of NT$10,000 to NT$50,000 (approximately USD 320 to 1,600) per item under the Taiwan Company Act Article 20(4). Continued noncompliance for more than one fiscal year authorizes the MOEA to administratively strike off or dissolve the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and Settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 May of the following calendar year for the preceding fiscal year (i.e., 31 May 2026 for FY 2025)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file is penalized at 10% of the tax due (minimum NT$1,500) plus monthly interest at the postal savings rate. Underpayment caused by negligence or fraud may trigger an additional penalty of 15% to 20% of the understated tax. The tax authority may attach bank deposits or movable assets, but strike-off is not directly triggered.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Confirmation and Roster Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (Central Registration, Company UBO Roster)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: An annual confirmation statement must be filed by 15 July for a 31 December fiscal year end, and in all cases within 30 days after any change in beneficial ownership, control, or senior management details; a nil return is mandatory if no change occurred
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under the Taiwan Money Laundering Control Act, failure to file or updating untimely incurs an administrative fine of NT$50,000 to NT$500,000 (approximately USD 1,550 to 15,600) per violation, plus a continuing monthly penalty of NT$5,000. Repeated violations may cause the MOEA to revoke company registration and initiate administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Taiwan Company Act Article 20 and the MOEA Regulations Governing the Scope of Companies Required to Have Financial Statements Audited by Certified Public Accountants, an independent certified CPA audit is legally mandatory if any of the following quantitative thresholds is met or exceeded at fiscal year-end: (i) paid-in capital of NT$30,000,000 (approximately USD 960,000); (ii) total assets of NT$300,000,000 (approximately USD 9,600,000); (iii) annual net operating revenue of NT$100,000,000 (approximately USD 3,200,000); or (iv) the company is a public limited company, a securities issuer, or operates in a regulated industry such as banking, insurance, or bill finance. The tax authority may also demand a certified audit under the Income Tax Act where deemed necessary for tax verification.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared in accordance with Taiwan Financial Reporting Standards (T-FRS), which are substantially converged with IFRS as endorsed by the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC). Non-public companies may elect to apply the SME framework (T-FRS for SMEs), which is aligned with IFRS for SMEs. Tax filings remain governed by the Income Tax Act and its Enforcement Rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Taiwan's Company Act and Money Laundering Control Act, the company must maintain a beneficial ownership register and file UBO details with the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 days of any shareholding transfer, change in control, or appointment/removal of senior managers. On an annual basis, no later than 15 July (for a 31 December fiscal year end), the company must file a UBO confirmation statement (nil return permitted if no changes), confirming the accuracy of the standing register. Failure to comply triggers escalating fines and, after repeated noncompliance, may lead to administrative strike-off of the company's registration.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 to 2,000 per year, depending on the service provider, city location, and inclusion of physical office address handling or mail forwarding.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 to 12,000 for a low-risk digital design subscription agency of the indicated size, depending on transaction volume, bookkeeping quality, and the tier of the CPA firm.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Low-Profit Enterprise income below RMB 3 million is effectively taxed at 5% (25% reduction then 20%); High-Tech Enterprise status may grant a 15% preferential rate; no additional Free-Trade Zone CIT reduction applies to the design-subscription business.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A100000 – Annual Corporate Income Tax (CIT) Return for Resident Enterprises (A-class) filed through the State Taxation Administration Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return with quarterly provisional payments (Form A200000 within 15 days after each quarter-end)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual CIT return must be filed within five months after the end of the taxable year, i.e. by May 31 for a calendar-year taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross design-subscription and UI/UX service revenue on a worldwide basis. For subscription payments routed via Stripe/Wise to the Taiwan parent, verify whether the Taiwan entity is an agent or a principal: if the WFOE remains the contracting principal, full revenue is recognized; if the Taiwan party performs services outside mainland China, consider the deductibility of service fees and PE exposure of the Taiwan party.

Capture direct design labor, software amortization, and subcontracted implementation costs. If a related-party cost-sharing or recharge arrangement with the Taiwanese shareholder exists, apply the arm's-length principle and retain full CUP/TNMM documentation for the cost allocation.
State surtaxes, stamp duty, and property-related taxes. Do not include income tax, VAT, or dividend withholding tax; non-deductible taxes (e.g., penalties, interest) must be removed in Box 8.

Include marketplace and payment rail fees (Stripe, Wise). Cross-border commission or referral fees paid to a Taiwan agent are subject to deeming rules at 10% of the payment amount if the Taiwan recipient is not treated as having a permanent establishment; ensure such expenses meet the business-related business vouchers requirement before deduction.

Management fees, brand charges, and headquarters costs recharged by the Taiwanese parent are deductible only if supported by a written service agreement, actual service performance evidence, and a cost-benefit analysis; the entry must be benchmarked against the PRC General Anti-Avoidance Rule before accepting the deduction.

Interest on shareholder loans is restricted by the 2:1 debt-to-equity thin capitalization rule; interest above the acceptable ceiling is non-deductible and must be added back. Withholding tax at 10% on the actual interest paid to the Taiwan lender must be remitted within 7 days of payment.

Impairment of receivables from foreign related parties (e.g., overdue subscription receivables from a Taiwan parent or affiliate) is generally disallowed unless the impairment is evidenced by formal internal evidence and an irrecoverability test; the addition back is required absent independent supporting proof.

This is the key reconciliation line. The WFOE must review Schedule A105000 for transfer pricing adjustments, intercompany expenditure recharacterizations, and disallowed overseas services charges. Any adjustment resulting in under-withholding of upstream taxes must be corrected with the proper penalties.

Net operating losses from previous years can offset up to five years of taxable income (ten years for qualifying High-Tech or small low-profit enterprises); if the Taiwan parent restructured the subscription revenue stream to curtail over-free loss carry-forwards, the tax bureau may deny the offset under the business purpose doctrine.

Headline 25% CIT on aggregate taxable income less tax credit and exemption items. Filigree with the consolidated quarterly prepayments; underpayment due to optimistic renaming of subscription receipts as a technology, branch, or procurement-related remission will expose the WFOE to late-filing surcharges and Article 63 penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual CIT return triggers a RMB 2,000 fine (up to RMB 10,000 in serious cases) under Article 62 of the Tax Collection and Administration Law (TCAL); late payment of tax carries a 0.05% daily surcharge on the overdue amount under TCAL Article 32. Intentional under-declaration of subscription revenue covering VAT and CIT over RMB 50,000 in criminal thresholds constitutes tax evasion, attracting a 50%-500% penalty under TCAL Article 63, and may lead to criminal proceedings under PRC Criminal Law Article 201 for the responsible director.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% (statutory) under EIT Law Article 37, applicable to after-tax profit distributions to the Taiwanese shareholder, unless a lower rate is granted under the not-yet-effective Cross-Strait Double Taxation Agreement (strait agreement).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Under the 2015 Cross-Strait Tax Agreement (not currently in force), the dividend withholding rate would be 5% where the Taiwanese beneficial owner holds at least 25% of the capital of the mainland paying company, and 10% in other cases. To claim any DTA benefit upon its entry into force, the WFOE must obtain a Taiwan Tax Residency Certificate (Taiwan Ministry of Finance), complete the PRC DTA treatment application form (A03034 plus beneficial owner declaration), maintain evidence of the Taiwanese investor's substantive business activities, and demonstrate that the investor is the beneficial owner with no conduit or pass-through arrangement; given current non-ratification of the agreement, the statutory 10% rate and the full 10% withholding must be remitted.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on royalties and interest paid by the WFOE to the Taiwanese shareholder is 10% (EIT Law Article 37); as no DTA is currently effective, no reduced treaty rate is available. In addition, payments made in mainland China for royalties or service fees are subject to VAT at 6% (and a 12% local surcharge on VAT) and must be withheld by the WFOE when remitting to the Taiwanese payee.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File preparation is mandatory where annual related-party transaction amounts exceed RMB 40 million for provision of services (including UI/UX design subscription services) or RMB 100 million for intangible property transfers; Master File must be prepared where total related-party transactions reach RMB 1 billion in a single year, or where a foreign group parent's consolidated revenue exceeds RMB 5.5 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Although mainland China does not yet apply an Economic Substance Resolution in the style of the UAE, the PRC Tax Authorities will disallow treaty/statutory benefits, and will recharacterize transactions under the EIT Law Article 47 General Anti-Avoidance Rule, where an offshore Taiwan or Hong Kong conduit lacks the employees, assets, and decision-making capacity to perform the service. The Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) test requires that the Taiwanese recipient (or the mainland WFOE, as applicable) actually performs the design, management, and risk-taking functions in the jurisdiction in which the income is reported; mere invoicing or no-substance shareholding in Taiwan triggers the beneficial owner rejection doctrine (Announcement 2015 No. 60) and shields the mainland tax base from profit shifting.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Director directs that all UI/UX subscription fees from foreign users be wired to the Taiwan parent's bank account without invoicing by the WFOE, and excludes the subscription revenue from the annual CIT return; thereby evading the 25% corporate tax on the booked business income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: TCAL Article 63 imposes a penalty of 50% to 500% of the under-payed tax and the additional daily 0.05% late surcharge; the State Taxation Administration may bank levy the WFOE's Stripe and Wise settlements and re-assess the prior six years of revenue; where unpaid tax exceeds RMB 50,000, the case is referred under PRC Criminal Law Article 201, punishable in the most severe tier by imprisonment of three to seven years and a fine.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A court piercing the corporate veil allows the tax authority to seek personal restitution against the director for the unpaid CIT and penalties, and to place the director on the tax blacklist (exit blockage), freezing the individual's passport for a maximum of six years. A criminal conviction can lead to personal property seizure, a permanent travel ban, and a custodial sentence of up to seven years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: WFOE enters into an intercompany management and design-service fee agreement with the Taiwanese parent but fails to prepare the Local File and omit the statutory G-s Schedule (related-party transaction table) when the annual cross-border payment surpasses RMB 40 million in services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under TCAL Article 62, the tax bureau may impose a RMB 2,000 to 10,000 fine for the un-filed related-party disclosures, and may apply Article 44, making a punitive upward adjustment of the captive service fee to reflect arm's-length price; the deficiency is additionally subject to the 50%-500% penalty after a tax evasion recharacterization and a 0.05% daily interest surcharge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Once the transfer pricing adjustment is reclassified as evasion, the directors become personally liable for the adjusted tax and penalties; the individual is forbidden to leave the mainland without the approval of the tax bureau, and if the adjustment exceeds the RMB 100,000 criminal threshold for fraudulent claim over-payment, the director may be arrested for fraud and face up to five years of imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE is operated entirely by employees of the Taiwanese parent, while its corporate resolutions are fabricated, it has no dedicated office or decision-making staff, and it routes subscription profits to Taiwan through 'management charges' without any actual management service being performed on mainland soil.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authorities apply the General Anti-Avoidance Rules (EIT Law Article 47) and may recharacterize the Taiwanese entity's charging structure as a distribution of profits, disallowing the deduction in full, and levy the statutory 10% dividend withholding tax plus a 50%-500% adjusted penalty; in cases that include false invoices, the PRC Invoice Management Regulations impose a maximum fine of RMB 500,000 and possible forced dissolution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil exposes the director to personal liability for all CIT, WHT and surcharges; an exit ban (blacklist) assesses the director's personal bank accounts; if the veil-piercing is accompanied by cross-border fraud convictions, the director faces a prison sentence of seven to ten years in a serious-scale, cross-border setting.
